html:
Nueva Cádiz was a Spanish town on the small island of Cubagua, off the coast of Venezuela, built in the early 1500s to exploit rich pearl beds. It was one of the first Spanish towns in South America.

Columbus found pearls on this coast in 1498, and Spanish traders soon followed. Indigenous people, many brought as slaves from the Bahamas and the mainland, were forced to dive for oysters until they died of exhaustion. For a few decades Cubagua's pearls were among the most valuable goods Spain took from the Americas.

By the 1530s the beds were exhausted, and in 1541 an earthquake and tidal wave wrecked the town, which was abandoned. Its ruins are a national monument of Venezuela. Critics such as Bartolomé de las Casas wrote of the cruelty of the pearl fisheries, part of the early Spanish conquest of the Caribbean.
sum: Nueva Cádiz was a Spanish town on the small island of Cubagua, off the coast of Venezuela, built in the early 1500s to exploit rich pearl beds. It was one of the first Spanish towns in South America.
